items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: so Duke went out and met her and so she said, "Oh, I never heard no band like that.

ctx.x: Mountbatten so Sophie Tucker came over as soon as she come in, they introduced her, Miss Tucker's in the house. We played "Some of These Days." That was her big number then, written by this colored cat. I forget his name -- Shelton -- Shelton Thomas, he wrote that tune, and gave it to her and it made her famous, because she always mentioned it.

So we played her theme song, and then we went through our repertoire playing different numbers, so during the intermission she come backstage and go Duke, said Duke, I want you to meet some friends of mine so we could socialize all over the place, so Duke went out and met her and so she said, "Oh, I never heard no band like that. What do you call it the Cotton Club orchestra?" We did, you know, she said, "Oh, no, she said, if it were left to me I would call it the Aristocrats of Jazz." That's how we changed our…

So she said, "How would you like to come to London?" So Duke told her you could play all over Europe but no American bands played in London. You remember that, no American bands were allowed to play in London, so Duke said -- he still don't know who she is, so later on, that's Lady Mountbatten -- so she said, "Would you come to London? I would like for you to come to London. My people could hear you." So Duke said, "Oh, that would be fine."
